_note: Public, redacted text for each patch of v2 (v1 entries carried, plus v2's): the defect class and the kind of fix only. No target values, test parameters, formulas, function names or the conventions themselves (all eval data). The full rationale and evidence of each patch are in its payload file on /data, whose sha256 PATCHES.md records.

v1-72.6-tests.summary: Verified left the step with no test cases: add tests that do not depend on the random stream
v1-72.6-tests.why: Verified removed the original seeded tests (an RNG-protocol defect) and left zero tests, so a do-nothing implementation passes. The new tests check limits with deterministic outcomes, plus an exact-enumeration statistical check that any valid random stream passes.

v1-50.1-tests.summary: Replace an over-lenient statistical test with a deterministic limit check and exact-enumeration statistical checks
v1-50.1-tests.why: Verified's single test compared a Monte Carlo average with another Monte Carlo estimate, inside a window several times too wide, so wrong-temperature and quench implementations pass. The new checks compare against exact Boltzmann averages of a small instance, within a few standard errors.

v1-60.3-tests.summary: Replace a test that cannot see the temperature convention with exact-valued statistical tests at two temperatures
v1-60.3-tests.why: Verified's one test at a single temperature cannot tell the correct temperature dependence from a common inverted one, and it also accepts a potential convention that the previous step excludes. The new tests use a configuration whose expectation is known exactly, at two temperatures.

v1-62.5-tests.summary: Add truncating cases checked by basis-invariant quantities, so a skipped or wrong basis transform fails
v1-62.5-tests.why: Verified rightly switched to basis-invariant checks, but its only case does not truncate, so any orthogonal transform passes, including the identity. The new cases truncate at gaps in the spectrum, where the kept subspace is unique.

v1-67.6-tests.summary: Restore a tight numeric-vs-analytic consistency check, and add one more case
v1-67.6-tests.why: Verified loosened this check by several orders of magnitude, which lets a known wrong-physics implementation pass (it failed the original). The audit measured every valid form far inside the restored tolerance, and the wrong one far outside it.

v1-76.4-text.summary: Make the window score use the same probability convention as the patched 76.2
v1-76.4-text.why: This keeps the 76.4 tests consistent with the convention stated by v1-76.2-text. Without it, one natural reading of the patched 76.2 fails a 76.4 test. Tests unchanged.

v1-76.2-tests.summary: Verified's own test cases and targets, registered so the build validates the patched convention
v1-76.2-tests.why: Verified's 76.2 targets encode a convention its text does not state, which contradicts 76.1 (the #184 contradiction). The targets are kept bit-for-bit and recomputed independently; v1-76.2-text states the convention. This patch makes the build check that the literal reading fails and that other valid implementations pass.

v1-55.4-tests.summary: Restore the value checks Verified dropped as 'chaotic', with regenerated targets
v1-55.4-tests.why: The audit shows the dynamics are not chaotic. The original targets carry a defect of the gold itself. Targets are regenerated from a reference that 55.1's own tests already pin, and every valid loop form passes.

v1-72.9-text.summary: State the two conventions the target needs scientifically instead of dictating code
v1-72.9-text.why: Verified pinned two load-bearing conventions correctly, but wrote them as the literal implementation. The new wording keeps both and drops the code.

v1-55.3-text.summary: Keep the load-bearing binning and peak conventions, drop the transcribed code
v1-55.3-text.why: The frozen targets need specific binning and peak-window conventions, so these stay. Verified also spelled out library calls and an explicit formula, which hand over the implementation.

v1-66.1-text.summary: Describe the lattice convention geometrically instead of listing the vectors
v1-66.1-text.why: The tests need one specific choice among several valid parameterisations, so the choice must be stated, but Verified gave the full construction as coordinates. The new wording fixes the same choice and leaves the derivation to the solver.

v1-71.2-text.summary: State the operand-order convention without naming the library call
v1-71.2-text.why: Only the order is a convention; the library call names the implementation.

v1-37.3-text.summary: Drop a docstring sentence that states a test's expected outcome
v1-37.3-text.why: The sentence gives away the asserted result and the sign of every target. The sign convention is already fixed elsewhere in the step.

v1-73.1-text.why: Cosmetic. Verified removed the same marker elsewhere (69-d1). No grading effect.

v1-69.3-text.why: Cosmetic. Verified made the identical fix in the sibling problem 67. No grading effect.

v1-68.6-text.summary: State the conventions the target needs instead of the closed-form result the step must compute
v1-68.6-text.why: Computing this quantity is the step's whole job, and Verified wrote out the result. The new wording keeps the conventions it needs and the definitions it follows from.

v1-55.2-text.summary: State the layout and normalization conventions mathematically instead of as library one-liners
v1-55.2-text.why: The conventions are load-bearing and stay; the library calls hand over the implementation.

v1-45.3-text.summary: Keep the stencil convention, drop the solved update that Verified added
v1-45.3-text.why: The solved update follows uniquely from the stated convention and is the step's job.

v1-79.3-text.summary: Keep the scheme choice, let the solver derive its coefficients
v1-79.3-text.why: Several schemes of this order exist, so naming the scheme is load-bearing. Its coefficients follow uniquely and are part of what the step asks the solver to know.

v1-80.5-text.summary: Replace the literal loop body with the physical statement
v1-80.5-text.why: The pair sum and the displacement direction are the conventions. The loop body is code.

v1-32.2-text.summary: No background: move the conventions the target needs into the prompt
v1-32.2-text.why: Without background, the prompt does not fix the constants and conventions the frozen target needs. Several were only in the background, some added there by Verified. They are stated physically, and the derivable quantities are left to the solver.

v1-22.2-text.summary: No background: state the convention that Verified added only to the background
v1-22.2-text.why: The target depends on a convention a solver cannot infer from the prompt. A different common convention changes signs and fails.

v1-55.1-text.summary: No background: state the numerical scheme the frozen target uses
v1-55.1-text.why: The prompt names only the method family, and variants of it differ from the target at first order in the step size. The scheme is stated; the operators are left to derive.

v1-60.2-text.summary: No background: state the cutoff convention (Verified fixed it only in the background)
v1-60.2-text.why: The prompt and header never say which convention applies, and the other one fails a test.

v1-63.3-text.summary: No background: state the discretization scheme whose coefficients the target holds
v1-63.3-text.why: Other standard schemes give a different matrix. The coefficients are left for the solver to derive.

v1-74.1-text.summary: No background: state the sign convention and the square-case convention the target needs
v1-74.1-text.why: The result is unique only up to signs. Verified added the deciding convention to the background only.

v1-76.2-text.summary: No background: state the convention the regenerated target encodes
v1-76.2-text.why: Verified's regenerated 76.2 targets assume a convention its text does not state, which contradicts the literal reading of 76.1's output (the #184 contradiction). Stating it keeps Verified's targets and changes only text.

v1-80.3-text.summary: No background: replace an undefined term with the definition the target uses
v1-80.3-text.why: Verified corrected the definition only in the background. Without background, the prompt's term has two wrong readings, and one test separates them.

v1-63.1-tests.summary: Fix test calls that pass two bounds in the wrong order; regenerate the targets
v1-63.1-tests.why: The 63.1/63.2/63.4 test cases pass two arguments swapped with respect to the signature, which reverses the grid and turns the boundary conditions into wrong finance. The later steps and the main-problem tests already use signature order. The regenerating reference reproduces every Verified target of 63.1-63.6 when called as Verified does.

v1-63.2-rows-text.summary: Restore the physical labels of the boundary rows, which are correct again after the argument-order fix
v1-63.2-rows-text.why: Verified had removed them because its tests reversed the grid.

v2-11.5-tests.summary: Over-strict test: the step compared one ordered representation of an object that is defined only up to equivalence; the tests now compare the object itself
v2-11.5-tests.why: Equivalent representations of the same channel (another order, another valid set) failed. The new check accepts exactly the equivalent ones, and every wrong channel still fails.

v2-11.5-text.summary: Underdetermined spec: the meaning of a model parameter was stated only in the background
v2-11.5-text.why: Several standard readings of the parameter give different channels at the tested points, and only the background fixed which one the targets use. The prompt now states it.

v2-13.8-text.summary: Underdetermined spec: several standard boundary conditions fit the prompt and the tests accept only one
v2-13.8-text.why: The background itself says the condition can be implemented in different ways, and the standard alternatives fail. The prompt now states which physical assumption applies, not how to implement it.

v2-22.1-text.summary: Underdetermined spec: the prompt gave only a magnitude where the target depends on a direction
v2-22.1-text.why: The opposite direction negates some targets exactly, and only the background's starting value fixed it. The prompt now fixes the direction.

v2-22.3-text.summary: Underdetermined spec that contradicts an earlier step: define the requested quantity and its direction convention, which only the background fixed
v2-22.3-text.why: The requested coefficients were never defined. Taking the direction convention of the earlier step reverses the sign of every target. The prompt now defines the quantity; the method is not given.

v2-33.1-text.summary: Underdetermined spec whose tests pick one of several valid conventions: state the conventions the target needs, without the matrix the step asks for
v2-33.1-text.why: The tests compare a full matrix, which depends on conventions (orientation, sublattice order, gauge, sign) set only in the background. Several equally valid choices fail.

v2-39.1-text.summary: Underdetermined spec whose tests pick one of several valid conventions: state the convention the target needs
v2-39.1-text.why: Several conventions give matrices with the same physics, and only some pass. One test cannot tell them apart.

v2-31.3-tests.summary: Over-strict tests whose outcome depended on the random initialization: score against ground truth, replace an ill-posed case, keep the threshold
v2-31.3-tests.why: The prescribed algorithm passed one case only for some random starts, and another case was scored against an earlier estimate rather than the true sources. The threshold is unchanged; the false-fail rate is measured in the payload.

v2-43.1-header-text.summary: Interface mismatch: the tests call the function in a form the documented interface did not allow; correct the documented argument shapes
v2-43.1-header-text.why: An implementation that follows the documented interface with correct physics crashes on the tests' calls.

v2-43.1-text.summary: Underdetermined spec: an input quantity has several standard definitions and the tests encode one; state the definition
v2-43.1-text.why: A complete implementation using the other common definition fails. The definition appeared only in later material.

v2-48.4-text.summary: Underdetermined convention: the theorem the step relies on has several normalizations and the tests encode one; state the normalization only
v2-48.4-text.why: Implementations using other standard normalizations fail. Only the normalization is stated; the relation the step derives is not.

v2-48.4-tests.summary: Inconsistent tolerance: a downstream check was stricter than the upstream steps whose accepted alternative it consumes; match the upstream tolerance, targets unchanged
v2-48.4-tests.why: Verified deliberately accepts an alternative in the earlier steps of this problem, and this step consumes their outputs. A fully valid implementation using that alternative failed here only on tolerance. The new tolerance equals the upstream one, and the wrong-physics mutants still fail.

v2-68.3-tests.summary: Over-lenient test: one method of the step's class was never exercised; add a direct check of it, mirroring the fix Verified made on the twin step
v2-68.3-tests.why: Wrong and zero implementations of that method passed, and later steps use it.

v2-28.1-tests.summary: Over-lenient test: only integrated sums were checked, so a mis-positioned output passed; add checks on the output's position and peak value
v2-28.1-tests.why: A wrong-physics result passes the original checks. Valid alternative methods still pass the new ones. Validated in one grading stack only: the problem's own dependency block cannot import in the other (documented, not changed).

v2-28.1-text.summary: Leak: Verified added the explicit formula the step should derive; keep the method choice, drop the formula
v2-28.1-text.why: The targets do not depend on the formula (an exact alternative also passes), so it fixed no convention and only handed over the physics.

v2-63.2-text.summary: Leak: the prompt dictated the whole step as literal assignments; state the conventions instead
v2-63.2-text.why: A verbatim copy of the given lines passed with no domain knowledge. The new text keeps every convention the targets need (grid layout, which boundary goes where, precedence).

v2-60.5-tests.summary: Infeasible runtime: shorten the run lengths of a test that checks an exact identity; targets and the statistical test unchanged
v2-60.5-tests.why: An implementation that follows the energy function the problem prescribes timed out on the official limit, mostly in a test whose expected value holds exactly at any run length. The statistical test is unchanged (shortening it would be unsafe); wrong-physics mutants still fail.

v2-80.7-tests.summary: Test rejects a valid answer: the statistical check also accepts a second, equally valid discretization
v2-80.7-tests.why: A standard exact discretization of the collision process biases the measured rate outside the window, although its physics is correct. The width is unchanged, and the wrong discretizations and wrong temperatures still fail.

v2-79.2-text.summary: Background-only convention: name the integration scheme the targets encode
v2-79.2-text.why: The targets are bit-exact to one splitting scheme, given only in the background. An exact integration and another symmetric splitting both fail. The prompt names the scheme, not its update equations.

v2-69.6-text.summary: Background-only convention: state the experimental geometry and normalization the targets assume
v2-69.6-text.why: Only one geometry and normalization reproduces the targets, and other valid readings fail. The prompt states the geometry, not the intensity formula.
